in_hebrew.name: יואקים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יואקים (יואקים) הוא שם נפחד. השם מוזכר בספר תענית (תענ. 1:12) כאחד מאבות ראשונים. בברית החדשה, יואקים (יואקים) הוא שם של אחד השבטאים של ישו (מתי 1:15).

in_greek.name: Ιωακείμ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ιωακείμ (Ιωακείμ) ήταν ένας από τους πατέρες της Μήτσελ (Ματθ. 1:15). Ο όρος φέρεται να ερμηνεύεται ως 'ο εστι για τον Κυριον'.

in_latin.name: Joaquim
in_latin.long_meaning: Joaquim nomen Christianum est, quod a Ioakim in lingua Hebraica ortum est. In Biblia, Ioakim unus ex patriarchis est qui in Genealogia Jesu Christi apparuit (Matt. 1:15).

in_english.name: Joaquim
in_english.meaning: Christian name with Hebrew origin, means 'he will cause the Lord to increase'
in_english.long_meaning: Joaquim is a Christian name with Hebrew origin, meaning 'he will cause the Lord to increase'. In the Bible, Joaquim is one of the ancestors of Jesus Christ mentioned in the Gospel of Matthew (Matthew 1:15). This name is also associated with Saint Joaquim, a 13th-century saint from Portugal. In Christian tradition, the name Joaquim is often given to children born in times of economic growth or prosperity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Joaquim holds significant cultural richness within Christian communities, particularly in Portugal and Brazil. In the Iberian Peninsula, Joaquim is considered an old and traditional name, and it was quite popular during the Middle Ages. In present-day Portugal, it's common to find many people with the name Joaquim, especially among those whose ancestors have roots in the rural areas. Joaquim is also a common name in Brazil, with a strong presence among Brazilians of African descent, particularly in regions like Bahia and Minas Gerais. The name is often associated with important religious and cultural events in these communities, much like how St. Joseph, another popular Joaquim variant "José," is an essential figure in both Portuguese and Brazilian traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Joaquim holds deep spiritual meaning as it comes from the Hebrew name Yo'akim, which can be translated to 'God will raise up'. This is a reassuring and powerful reminder of God's omnipotence, as it conveys the idea that even when we are facing difficult situations, God is always present and will support us in our time of need. Through the biblical characters associated with the name Joaquim, such as Eliakim the high priest, the name also represents the importance of spiritual leadership and service to God. Ultimately, the name Joaquim serves as a constant reminder that, no matter the challenges we may face, God is always with us, and He will raise us up.
